title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 37
statement: Call a positive integer "mild" if its base-3 representation never contains the digit 2 . How many values of \(n(1 \leq n \leq 1000)\) have the property that \(n\) and \(n^{2}\) are both mild?

solutions.text: 7 Such a number, which must consist entirely of 0 's and 1 's in base 3, can never have more than one 1. Indeed, if \(n=3^{a}+3^{b}+\) higher powers where \(b>a\), then \(n^{2}=3^{2 a}+2 \cdot 3^{a+b}+\) higher powers which will not be mild. On the other hand, if \(n\) does just have one 1 in base 3, then clearly \(n\) and \(n^{2}\) are mild. So the values of \(n \leq 1000\) that work are \(3^{0}, 3^{1}, \ldots, 3^{6}\); there are 7 of them.
